guarantees.claim: key_sideload[s][i] is continuously driven as a 32-bit slice from keymgr_key_i.key[s], starting at bit i*32, with no combinatorial masking or modification.

assumptions.claim: keymgr_key_i.key must have dimensions matching NumSharesKey and NumRegsKey, providing at least (NumRegsKey*32) bits per share, so that the slice [i*32+:32] is always within bounds.
assumptions.cond: whenever this combinational block is evaluated
assumptions.risk: If keymgr_key_i.key has insufficient width for the given NumRegsKey, the out-of-bounds bit-select will produce X or undefined values, corrupting key_sideload.

assumptions.claim: keymgr_key_i must be a stable, glitch-free side-loaded value; the chunk assumes that any upstream key delivery already handles clearing, masking, or secure transport.
assumptions.cond: during active use of the key_sideload value downstream
assumptions.risk: A glitch, timing violation, or erroneous update on keymgr_key_i could expose an unmasked secret key value into key_sideload and downstream logic, breaking confidentiality.

uncertain_points.claim: key_sideload is driven by direct combinatorial assignment of keymgr_key_i with no masking, clearing, or secret-sharing within this chunk. It is unclear whether downstream logic applies masking before cryptographic use, or if this direct path violates side-channel resistance requirements.
uncertain_points.cond: key_sideload is used by subsequent AES datapath
uncertain_points.risk: Raw secret key could be observable in unencrypted form inside the design, increasing side-channel leakage or direct extraction risk.

uncertain_points.claim: The stability, timing, and driving context of keymgr_key_i outside this chunk are not visible. It is unknown whether the input is registered, synchronized, or may change during an active encryption.
uncertain_points.cond: when aes_core uses key_sideload for round key expansion or cipher operations
uncertain_points.risk: If keymgr_key_i can change asynchronously, key_sideload will glitch and may cause incorrect cipher output or expose intermediate key values.

uncertain_points.claim: The parameter NumRegsKey directly controls the bit slice offset. If a legal parameterization sets NumRegsKey larger than the actual keymgr_key_i.key width, out-of-bounds access occurs.
uncertain_points.cond: when NumRegsKey is configured beyond the producer's key width
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect key expansion, X propagation, or silent use of truncated/shifted key data.
